text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Malaysian government accepts Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's unreserved apology, but says restoration of old level relationship between both countries will take time.
- Singapore notes Malaysian statement but expresses surprise at statement that restoration of old level of ties will take time.
- Hong Leong group executive chairman Kwek Leng Beng named Singapore's Businessman of the Year.
- Thailand Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh names Singapore as one of country's vital economic partners.
- Orang-utan develops a crush on her London psychologist.
- Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan announces government will award another two mobile phone licences to cellular operators.
- Audio-tape maker General Magnetics losses from Singapore rise from $1.1 million in 1995 to Singapore $3.66 million in 1996.
- Stock Exchange of Singapore criticises three Jumabhoy family Scotts Holdings directors and asks company to ensure sufficient majority of independent directors to safeguard minority shareholders.
- Hotel Royal revalues Newton Road property and proposes 2-for-3 bonus.
- Mainboard-listed Orchard Parade Holdings announces net earnings of Singapore $24.82 million last year, a 110 percent increase.
- Telecommunications and electronics firm Acma Ltd experiences 23 percent profit decline to Singapore $40.59 million in 1996.
